answer: The MCP `lua` tool needs the Runtime API. A headless Chrome instance runs the code, driven over Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). In multi-space mode an admin switches it on with the **Enable runtime API** toggle in the Dashboard's **APIs** tab. (Source: `MCP.md` and `Runtime API.md`.)

MCP.md:46:Any client that speaks Streamable HTTP MCP and supports OAuth 2.1 should work. A client identifies itself with a client ID metadata document (an https URL as its client ID) or registers dynamically. Most clients are public and rely on PKCE alone; a client whose metadata document registers `private_key_jwt` (as ChatGPT does) must also sign a client assertion at the token endpoint with a key from its published JWKS (RS256, PS256 or ES256).
MCP.md:49:SilverBullet Desktop serves MCP too, for the spaces registered in the app, on a loopback listener at `http://127.0.0.1:3999/.mcp`. It is off by default. Turn it on or change the port under **Settings → Advanced → MCP**, which also shows the setup commands with your port filled in.

7:The Runtime API lets you interact with a SilverBullet client programmatically via HTTP.
9:Requests are evaluated via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) in a headless Chrome instance, which does the actual execution so all results reflect the live client state.
12:> The [[CLI]] provides a convenient command-line interface for the Runtime API — evaluate Lua, run scripts, and more, without writing raw HTTP requests.
15:> Searching the space does not need the Runtime API: see [[HTTP API#Search]].
18:The Runtime API is enabled automatically when Chrome, Chromium, or Chromium headless shell is detected on your system — no configuration needed. Auto-detection prefers headless shell when it is available on `PATH`.
20:If Chrome is not auto-detected, for some reason, set the path explicitly:
22:SB_CHROME_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium
25:In single-instance mode, set `SB_RUNTIME_API=0` to disable the Runtime API, and `SB_RUNTIME_IDLE_TIMEOUT` to change when an idle runtime stops (see [[#Idle stop]]). In multi-space mode these variables are ignored: use the **Enable runtime API** toggle in the administrator’s **APIs** tab. Each writer has an independent **Runtime API** permission in the space’s access grid. Existing writers default to enabled unless explicitly opted out.
76:Returns recent console log entries from the headless browser.
151:Status codes used across the Runtime API:
153:* **403** — The caller lacks Write or Runtime API permission.
157:* **503** — Runtime API not enabled: `{"error": "Runtime API is not enabled"}`. This also holds when it is switched off for the running server (by an administrator or `SB_RUNTIME_API=0`), Chrome is missing, or the runtime pool failed to start. A headless browser that is not ready yet answers `{"error": "...", "code": "bridge_unavailable"}`; retry shortly.
163:When the Runtime API is enabled, the first request to an `/.runtime/` endpoint starts a separate headless Chrome process for that user and space. Each runtime has its own profile, cookies, browser storage, and console log. It loads the full SilverBullet client with the originating user’s identity and permissions. Removing Write or runtime access, disabling the account, or switching runtime off stops the affected browser and invalidates its credentials.
165:Once ready, the server communicates with the browser directly via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Because Lua code runs inside a real SilverBullet client, it has access to the full API surface — `editor.*`, `space.*`, queries, and everything else available to in-page scripts and widgets. The results reflect live client state.
168:A runtime that has received no requests for 30 minutes is stopped: its Chrome exits and it uses no memory or CPU. The next request starts it again on the same profile, so the client picks up where it left off instead of rebuilding its index. That takes about a second, plus the time to index pages that changed in the meantime.
177:Each user of a space has one Chrome profile, holding the client's index and browser storage. It is kept when the runtime stops (whether idle, by an administrator's **Stop**, or at server shutdown) and reused next time.
179:A profile is deleted on **Reset**, when the user loses Write or runtime access or their credentials change, when the Runtime API is switched off, and when the space is deleted.
181:Profiles live under `.chrome-data` in the server's data folder, or under `SB_CHROME_DATA_DIR` when set. Their directory names are hashes of the server folder, space and user.
184:Set `SB_CHROME_SHOW=1` to run Chrome with a visible window — useful for watching what the headless client is doing. Set `SB_CHROME_DATA_DIR` to choose the directory that holds the runtime profiles. Startup logs report the detected Chrome executable or that Chrome is unavailable.
187:Headless Chrome spawns several processes (browser, network, storage, and renderer) for each active user and space pair. Additional runtimes therefore cost a whole browser, not just a tab. Browsers start lazily so unused runtime permissions consume no Chrome processes, and stop again after a period without requests (see [[#Idle stop]]).
